ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The left side of the figure is marked with “sea” and “ocean,” indicating the ocean, and the right side is a land area; there is a latitude line marked 40° crossing the middle of the figure. The isotherms are generally distributed east-west, with 24℃ marked in the upper part, 20℃ marked near the middle, and 16℃ marked in the lower part, overall showing that temperature decreases from north to south. P is located near the land on the right side, and there is a local closed isotherm anomaly around it; the stem explains that this anomaly is affected by terrain. Then reason: When judging the month, first ignore the local anomaly at P caused by terrain, and analyze according to the overall isotherm distribution. In the figure, temperature decreases southward, indicating that the farther south one goes, the closer one is to the colder high-latitude direction, so this region should be located in the Southern Hemisphere. The overall temperature shown is relatively high, and the bending of the isotherms near the sea and land reflects that the Southern Hemisphere is in the warm season. The representative month of the warm season in the Southern Hemisphere is February, so this month is most likely February.
